title: Maynila
capsule: Maynila was a Tagalog Muslim polity seated on the southern bank of the Pasig River at its mouth, occupying the site of present-day Intramuros in Manila. Ruled by rajas of Malay-Hindu lineage who had converted to Islam, it functioned as a major redistribution hub for Chinese and Japanese trade goods reaching the Philippine archipelago. Spanish explorer Martín de Goiti took the settlement by force in 1570, and on 24 June 1571 Miguel López de Legazpi formally established the city of Manila on its ruins, ending the polity's independence. Rajah Sulayman III, who had burned Maynila before the final Spanish assault, was the last ruler to hold autonomous authority.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The settlement is well documented by Spanish accounts from 1570–71, but its pre-Spanish territorial extent and dynastic chronology rest largely on colonial-era transcriptions of oral tradition, leaving precise boundaries uncertain.
